slides.title: Debrief Turns Individual Experience Into Shared Knowledge
bullets: Without a structured debrief, most congress value stays scattered
It lives only in each MSL's personal notes and memory
That value fades progressively over the following weeks

slides.title: Debrief Reaches Beyond the Field Team
bullets: MSLs and Medical Affairs leadership at minimum
Medical strategy teams as well
Commercial or market access teams, when formal non-confidential channels justify it
This ensures insights flow into wider organizational decisions

slides.title: Five Blocks Every Debrief Should Cover
bullets: Scientific coverage: what was covered, what was missed, and why
Insight summary, prioritized by strategic impact, not chronology
Competitive intelligence from public sources, properly channeled
KOL and DOL relationship review: new contacts, strengthened ties, commitments
Research collaboration or evidence generation opportunities identified

slides.title: A Good Debrief Connects Facts to Decisions
bullets: Not just documenting what happened
Naming which insights need immediate follow-up action
Naming which relationships need a specific cultivation plan
Spelling out what competitive intelligence means for product positioning

slides.title: Asynchronous Tools Keep the Debrief Flowing
bullets: Shared documents, insight platforms, and team messaging channels help
No need to find one common slot for the whole team right after the congress
Information can flow continuously, even while some are still traveling back

takeaway.title: The debrief is what converts one congress into knowledge the whole organization can use
bullets: It needs a cross-functional audience, not just the field team
A fixed structure keeps insights prioritized instead of just listed
Its value comes from linking findings to concrete next actions
